articleTitle: Photonic Crystal Fiber based Surface Plasmon Resonance Bio- Sensors with bimetallic selectively filled metal layers
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) bio-sensor with bimetallic selectively filled metal layers is proposed. Single mode PCF excites the plasmons on the inner surface of the selectively filled metalized nanolayers of gold and silver. Finite Element Method (FEM) with perfectly matched layer (PML) is applied to evaluate the complex propagation constant. The sensor consists of selectively filled metalized air holes analyte channel with silver and gold which provide the two sensitive plasmonic peaks corresponds to each metal layer so the proposed sensor can be used as a multimolecule sensing for the single analyte

articleTitle: Micro mechanical deformation sensor based on ultra sensitive photonic crystal membrane
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the proposed work photonic crystal silicon slab type structure is analyzed with two photonic crystal configuration in line defect with micro cavity in water and air medium for monitoring strain sensing capacities of sensing layer. Pressure is applied and temperature of fluid such as air and water is increased from 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C to 31<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C. From the result it is observed that sensing structure shown better sensing capability in air compare to water. Maximum sensitivity of 0.34nm/RIU is obtained with Q factor of 2356 for holes in slab configuration of air medium. Proposed sensor having tremendous application in biomedical systems.

articleTitle: Real-time Accurate Monitoring of Ten Finger Joint Angles Using a Fiber Bragg Grating Sensor-based Glove for use in Virtual Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Virtual reality-based exercises being immersive and interactive have become a useful tool in the rehabilitation of stroke survivors. Input systems such as instrumented gloves used in VR systems must be accurate, highly repeatable, and have very low latency to make the VR environment immersive. This paper describes an FBG sensor-based glove that offers very high accuracy (error = 0.80°) and excellent repeatability (standard deviation = 0.95°) in measuring the ten finger joint angles of the human hand simultaneously. The accuracy and repeatability of six of these sensors attached on the glove were tested using a pre-calibrated inertial measurement unit sensor.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband Wide-Angle Metallo-Dielectric Metamaterial Absorber for Solar Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present analytical and numerical investigations revealing a new recipe of ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber, comprising a periodic 1D grating of a multilayered, alternating metal-dielectric, tapered structure. We report over 99% absorption using molybdenum (metal) - germanium (dielectric) layers at normal incidence in the visible and near-infrared regime of the solar radiation spectrum. The broadband absorption is attributed to multiple slow-wave modes getting absorbed at different layers. Additionally, our simulation model shows angle insensitivity up to 60 degrees. Absorbance spectra, obtained from effective medium theory, agree well with our simulation results. Potential applications can be solar energy harvesting and stealth technologies.

articleTitle: 2D Photonic Crystal Cantilever Resonator Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work the pressure sensor based two dimensional photonic crystal is proposed and designed with the high quality factor. The sensor is formed by coupling of two photonic crystal waveguides and one nanocavity. A rectangular structure with the triangular lattice of air holes in slab type photonic crystal is considered and the point defect is placed at the centre. For the radius of the holes, optimization is carried out for high Q factor. For the radius of a hole at 165 nm, Q factor obtained is 5355.93.The photonic crystal structure with radius of hole as 165 nm is considered for pressure sensor application.The Refractive index values of the material are calculated for different pressures. Normalized transmission with wavelength shift for different pressure is observed. Through simulation it is noticed that the resonant wavelength of the sensor is shifted linearly towards highest region while increasing the applied pressure. This simulation and analysis is done by software called FDTD Lumerical solution. And the best quality factor is achieved.

articleTitle: Identification of the calcified tissues using laser induced breakdown spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report the recognition of male and female teeth samples using Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) technique. A multivariate method, principal component analysis (PCA) has been employed for discrimination. Our results have demonstrated an excellent separation between the samples even though it has a similar chemical composition. These findings will show an immediate impact in the field of archeology and forensic science application.

articleTitle: Characteristics of transient underwater acoustic signal from laser-induced plasma formation
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The characteristics of underwater acoustic emissions from optical breakdown due to 30 ps laser pulses in both time and frequency domain are presented. The time-frequency analysis reveals that the frequency and arrival time of underwater acoustic impulse maintain simultaneity.

articleTitle: Statistical interpretation of Mueller matrix images of spatial light modulator
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present an experimental and quantitative study of Mueller matrix images of a reflective type spatial light modulator (SLM). We capture 16 Mueller matrix images at various gray values of SLM using Mueller matrix imaging polarimeter (MMIP). These Mueller matrix images have been analysed by using probability density function (PDF) plots and corresponding central moment parameters have been determined. The obtained results indicate that the central moment parameters are sensitive to the various gray values of SLM and can be used to characterize the polarimetric response of liquid crystal (LC) devices.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Explosive Materials mixed in Teflon Matrix in THz regime
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Most of the materials in the real-life situation are opaque in Terahertz (THz) regime so it is not easy to study the materials transmission properties. Moreover, it becomes more challenging when it is located at remote distance. Therefore, reflection data provides solution for detection of explosive materials in standoff mode. The paper reports the study of the reflection coefficient, refractive index, absorption coefficients and optical impedance of premium explosives like RDX, TNT and Ammonium Nitrate (NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) mixed in Teflon matrix using time-domain THz spectroscopy. The reflection coefficient ascertained using a modified Fresnel equation.

articleTitle: A side-polished macro bend fiber sensor for the efficient Detection of petrol adulteration
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A side-polished macro bend fiber sensor is fabricated and demonstrated here. The working principle is based on the macro bending loss and evanescent field absorption. A sensitivity of 90nW/% and 45nW/% are obtained for low and high level of adulteration respectively.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg Grating Based Ice Detection Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: One of the main issues concerning flight safety is ice formation. The formation of ice can take place anywhere on an aircraft surface including engines and air induction systems during snow, freezing rain, hail, super cooled fog, or frost. The formation of ice can occur in many ways such as rime ice, glaze ice, runback ice, and mixed ice. The impact of icing on the aircraft results in loss of aerodynamic efficiency, engine power, control surface efficiency, engine failure and increase in fuel consumption. This work presents the detection and monitoring of ice formation using fiber-optic sensing techniques.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Resonance Based Carbon Monoxide Sensor Utilizing ZnO Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose ZnO grating/Au film based SPR sensor for the detection of carbon monoxide. Numerical simulations based on rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA) are performed to analyze the performance of the sensor. Grating depth of the sensor has also been optimized for quality factor. With optimized grating depth, we could achieve the quality factor of 0.21 per ppm. We also show that quality factor can further be enhanced to 0.29 per ppm by using Ag film underneath ZnO grating.

articleTitle: Single-Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometer based Detection of Fluoride Ion Contamination in Water
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The fabricated single-fiber (SF) MZI was used for the detection of contamination of fluoride ion concentration in drinking water at ppm level over a concentration range of 0 ppm to 2.5 ppm. The report is based on the study of shift in notch wavelength of SF-MZI with the change in refractive index and the sensitivity was recorded 228.6 pm per ppm.

articleTitle: Thin Film Sensing with Asymmetric Terahertz Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate asymmetric terahertz metasurfaces for thin film sensing. The asymmetric SRR based metasurface design is observed to excite a sharp Fano-like dark mode resonance which is not seen in the corresponding symmetric SRR based design. The simulated transmission characteristics show a close match with the experimental results. Sensitivity and Figure of Merit have been calculated for both the sensor designs and it is observed that the Fano-identical dark mode resonance in the asymmetric SRR based metasurface is highly suitable for thin film sensing due to its high FoM value.

articleTitle: Information Encryption in Thermal Metamaterials by Emissivity Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Optically transparent metamaterial structures have been designed with customized spectral emissivity response across the technologically important Long Wave Infrared (LWIR) window by utilizing a structure that is amenable for large-area manufacturing. Such metamaterial structures can be instrumental in information security and IR tagging applications.

articleTitle: Stand-off Femtosecond Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy of Metals, Soil, Plastics and Classification Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The femtosecond stand-off laser induced breakdown spectroscopy (fs ST-LIBS) experiment is optimized for 5m distance. The fs ST-LIBS spectra of metals, alloys, soil, organic samples are recorded. Most of the atomic peaks and molecular peaks like CN, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and Aluminum oxide are identified from the characteristic emission lines in the spectra. The signal to noise ratio is reduced compared to the near field case. The similarities existing in the spectral emission lines collected from different targets limits the technique for identification. We have used principal component analysis (PCA) which improves the identification and classification of the materials used as targets.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Waveguide Based Optical Ring Resonator For Bio-sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The main aim of this work is to design and analyze a highly sensitive and miniaturized plasmonic ring resonator biosensor. Enhancement in field confinement due to plasmonic effect results in a considerable field confinement at the interface between metal (gold) and dielectric i.e. in the slot region. Hence, for this structure an average index sensitivity of 860 nm/RIU has been observed. Finite Element Method has been used for designing and performance analysis, investigated for the biological refractive index window of 1.34-1.35.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of pi-Phase-Shifted Fiber Bragg Grating for Longitudinal Ultrasonic Acoustic Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis of pi-phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating (π-FBG) for longitudinal ultrasonic (US) acoustic stain wave. The influence of grating controlling parameters (grating length, index change, and apodization), and US acoustic wavelengths on the wavelength-shift sensitivity of the π-FBG has been investigated. The effect of the slow-light in the π-FBG acoustic sensor has also been discussed. Simulation results show that apodization reduces the sensitivity of the π-FBG acoustic sensor. Coupled mode theory (CMT) and transfer matrix method (TMM) have been employed to simulate the spectral characteristics of π-FBG.

articleTitle: Realization of all optical J-K flipflops in mid-IR wavelengths Using Triple-core Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We design the GeAsS triple-core photonic crystal fiber (TPCF) to obtain the efficient all-optical J-K flipflop in mid-infrared (IR) wavelength. Non-linearity and dispersion of proposed fiber is calculated at input wavelength of 3.1 μm. The evolution of pulse propagation is modelled using coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations. Our results exhibit that the proposed GeAsS triple core PCF is good candidate to acts an all optical memory devices in mid-IR wavelengths.

articleTitle: Broadband THz transmission characteristics of common polymers and semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report in house development of a Fourier Transform Spectrometer working in the terahertz (THz) frequency range (FTS-THz) using two color ultra-short laser produced plasma as broadband (0.1 - 60 THz) source of THz radiation. The FTS is used to characterize the broadband transmission characteristic of common polymers (Teflon (PTFE) and low density poly-ethylene (LDPE)) and semiconductors (Silicon and Gallium Arsenide). Employing broadband means of THz generation and detection provides for a thorough characterization of the sample material and enables identification of several spectral features over a large frequency range.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bandwidth of Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Effect in Two-dimensional Terahertz Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: It is known that metamaterials are showing rich electromagnetic induced transparency (EIT) like effect due to the superposition of brighter and darker modes present in MTM structures. Several works have reported EIT-like effect for manipulating polarized states and creating delay line and filters for various electromagnetic frequencies ranging from microwaves to visible light. In this work, MTM formed by L-shaped cut-wire is reported and the proposed material exhibits broadband EIT window over a bandwidth of 1.67 THz for transverse electric polarized light. The enhancement in the bandwidth of EIT effect is achieved by controlling the coupling between various resonating elements presented in the design. Surface current analysis is carried out to explain the interaction between bright and dark modes of the proposed design. Since EIT-like effect is important in the realization of delay lines and filters, our proposed MTM may be suitable for the realization of terahertz devices.

articleTitle: Refractive Index based Biosensor using Photonic Quasi Crystal Fiber for Detection of Metastasis Tumor cells in brain
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a refractive index (RI) based biosensor using photonic quasi-crystal fiber to diagnose metastasis brain tumor cells. The fiber structure optimization is carried out by varying diameter of tumor cell cavity size and pitch in order to observe the wavelength shift. The performance of proposed RI based biosensor is analyzed by means of wavelength sensitivity and figure of merit (FoM). The proposed biosensor exhibits the ultra-high wavelength sensitivity as 2,15,827 nm/RIU and FoM is about 5497.19.

articleTitle: Evanescent field based Ethanol detection by using nanocomposite Bi doped ZnO thin film over modified clad fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Bi doped ZnO (BiZn) thin film was prepared by hydrothermal technique and thoroughly characterized using different material characterization techniques viz. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Ultraviolet and visible (UV) absorption, Photoluminescence (PL) spectra analysis and field emission scattering electron microscope (FESEM). As synthesized BiZn was deposited over modified clad optical fiber to extract evanescent wave. The developed BiZn coated optical fiber sensor was employed as ethanol sensor within 0-800 ppm range and exhibit sensitivity (%) 0.2588.

articleTitle: Sensitive Detection of Phase Separation with Femtosecond Thermal Lens Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Femtosecond Thermal Lens Spectroscopy (FTLS) has been developed to a level of sensitivity that can have molecule specific response due to convection as demonstrated experimentally and theoretically. Within this framework, we show here that it is possible to use this technique for sensitive detection of liquid versus gas phase. Experimental demonstration is made with a single beam FTLS experiment of traces of iodine in pentane mixture in liquid versus its vapor phase.

articleTitle: Signal to noise ratio enhancement in confocal microscope with an array detector
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Confocal microscopy is the most widely used imaging technique for producing high-resolution images of a specimen. Optical sectioning is possible due to the use of a pinhole in front of a point detector that obstructs all out of focus light coming from below and above the image plane. In this work, we have replaced the point detector with an array detector and studied the signal to noise ratio of images acquired by the developed microscope.

articleTitle: Simulation studies on the generation of 110 GHz mm-wave for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Stable and noise free generation of mm-wave demands the utilization of optical technology for the 5G communication networks. Radio-over-Fiber technology (RoF) is a favourable technology for the generation of mm-wave. In this paper, a simulation setup of the full duplex mm-wave RoF system comprising Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) has been developed and comparative analysis of noise and output signal power levels of different modulators has also been performed. Finally, generation of 110 GHz mm-wave using ElectroAbsorption Modulator (EAM) has been presented. The proposed system has the advantage of reusing the same wavelength in both uplink and downlink.

articleTitle: Optical Tamm Plasmon Based Biosensor in the Near Infrared Region
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Optical Tamm plasmon (OTP) based biosensor is proposed for detecting various blood constituents. The geometry which has been investigated theoretically is comprised of liquid cell sandwiched between a photonic crystal (PhC) and a thin metal film. The liquid cell is filled with blood components and traps light through the excitation of OTP mode. The OTP mode exhibits sharp absorption or transmission peaks in the high reflection band of the PhC. The OTP mode exhibits strong dispersive properties by virtue of significant presence of the field in the liquid cell and hence gives the signature of the blood constituents.

articleTitle: Sensing the Molecular Properties in Methanol and its Binary Mixtures using Time-Resolved Thermal Lens Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Mode Mismatched Pump-Probe spectroscopic method was employed to examine the thermally induced nonlinear optical properties of methanol and its binary mixtures. The heat transfer mechanism in methanol and its binary mixtures with carbon tetrachloride (CCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) at different concentrations of methanol is investigated. Methanol has the highest Thermal Lens (TL) signal, and CCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> does not have any TL signal at all. However, the presence of CCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> modulates the TL signal of the binary mixture. The time-domain shift in TL signal is observed for different concentrations of methanol, which indicates the unusual molecular behavior in the binary mixture.

articleTitle: Enhanced Lasing in Metal-Insulator-Metal Waveguide Slab based on Gold Coated Nanoporous Anodic Alumina Membrane
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We studied lasing in Rh6G dye infiltrated nanoporous anodic alumina membrane-based waveguide slab fabricated on top of an aluminum substrate. An amplifying liquid dye was circulated throughout the nanoporous alumina slab due to the wetting effect. A comparative study of lasing threshold on the 10 μm gold-coated portion of the nanoporous alumina (acting as a metal-insulator-metal waveguide) and bare alumina portion confirms the enhanced lasing emission in the former scenario. We also reduced the slab thickness to about 1.5 μm, and obtained stabilized lasing from gold coated alumina membrane.

articleTitle: Visible Wavelength Photonic Integrated Circuit in Silicon Nitride Platform for On-Chip Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present design and demonstration of visible light compatible silicon nitride waveguide and grating coupler for on-chip sensing applications.

articleTitle: Shadowgraphic Imaging of Cavitation Bubble Dynamics in Pulsed Laser Ablation of a Solid in Liquid
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Properties of nanoparticles synthesized via pulsed laser ablation of a solid target immersed in liquid are dependent to a great extent on the dynamics of the cavitation bubbles produced in the process. Hence, understanding the behavior of the cavitation bubbles is extremely important. Temporal evolution of the cavitation bubbles can be used to study its growth and also determine the extreme conditions prevailing within it. In the present work, shadowgraphic imaging technique is used to evaluate the velocity of the bubble and also the pressure and temperature inside it.

articleTitle: Design of 2.4X Dual Field of View MWIR (3-5µm) Zoom Lens
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A 2.4X thermal imaging mechanically compensated dual field of view zoom system for 3-5μm (MWIR) with cooled FPA detector with blur removal mechanism is designed. Use of Diffractive Optical Elements (DOE's) and Aspherics balances chromatic and monochromatic aberrations. In this work reimaging optics has been used to achieve 100% cold shield efficiency. Two folding mirror assembly is included inside the design to resolve image blurring induced by platform motions. The challenges associated with this additional mirror assembly and performance optimization are discussed in detail. The final optical layout with performance analysis and Lens movement are discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of Orbital Angular Momentum modes using Photonic Lanterns
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Photonic lanterns are novel photonic devices, which can be realized as an all-fiber device by an adiabatic taper of a single mode fiber (SMF) bunch arranged within a low index capillary. They are broadly classified based on the number of SMF cores and the functionality of mode selectivity. We present a detailed mathematical model to design and analyze generation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes using photonic lanterns. The effects of various design parameters like asymmetry and taper profile on the output OAM mode is discussed. Three and six core photonic lanterns have been used as examples for the study.

articleTitle: Development of picosecond standoff libs system for the identification of the metals and alloys
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report the development and optimization of a standoff laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (ST-LIBS) system for identification of metals and alloys. A simple convex lens and low-cost portable CCD spectrometer were utilized as collection system instead of conventional big telescope coupled to ICCD. Good signal to noise ratio has been achieved with minimum pulse energy of 2.5 mJ at a standoff distance of 6 m. This is the first report on picosecond ST-LIBS combined with compact detection system to the best of our knowledge. The developed system can work as a promising tool for process control and defense applications.

articleTitle: Simulation of Spectral Division Multiplexing For Monitoring Identical FBGs
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBGs) can be easily incorporated into sensor network for structural health monitoring. The FBGs in these networks can be monitored by various multiplexing techniques such as wavelength division multiplexing or time division multiplexing. However identical FBGs with overlapping spectra present in the network mask each other, and generally cannot be distinguished. In this paper, a new method of spectral division multiplexing is proposed which can monitor identical individual FBGs in a serial sensor network. The simulation results are presented below.

articleTitle: High-Speed Cavity Enhanced Silicon Photodetector on SiN-SOI Platform for Short Reach Optical Datacom
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate on-chip integrated, high-speed cavity-enhanced Silicon MSM photodetector on SiN-SOI platform for short-reach optical datacom at 850 nm wavelength. Silicon MSM photodetector is integrated inside a SiN ring resonator cavity. Compare to the conventional waveguide integrated photodetector the proposed device achieves 10X fold enhancement in responsivity at 850 nm wavelength. High-speed characterization of the proposed device is performed by capturing the impulse response of the device with illumination of femtosecond duration pulse laser at 850 nm wavelength. We measure 3dB bandwidth of 6.1 GHz which can be further be improved suitable for datacoms and supercomputers.

articleTitle: Ultra High Refractive Index Sensitivity using Directional Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a refractive index sensor employing an optical fiber directional coupler. An ultra-high sensitivity of 3908 nm/RIU was found to exist in the biological sample detection range 1.333-1.353. A theoretical study along with the experimental observations is presented.

articleTitle: Optical sectioning microscopy with both mechanical and non-mechanical beam scanning mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Optical sectioning microscopy is an important imaging technique best known for its ability to produce high contrast images of the specimen. Image is formed by scanning the focused illumination beam over the specimen plane normally with the help of a mechanical scanner. In this work, we have developed an optical sectioning microscope which has both mechanical as well as non-mechanical beam scanning mechanisms.

articleTitle: Ambient condition dependent surface plasmon resonance properties of pulsed laser deposited ITO thin films
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this report, surface plasmon resonance properties of pulsed laser deposited ITO thin films are studied both experimentally and theoretically in the presence of two different ambient conditions, namely - high vacuum and 0.001 mbar of N2 gas pressure. These conditions can effectively tune the cutoff wavelength from 1280 nm to 1368 nm, while shifting the surface plasmon resonance position from 1293 nm to 1448 nm. Experimentally obtained peak positions and full-width-at-half- maxima of the angle-dependent reflectivity spectra matches significantly with the simulated spectra using transfer matrix method.

articleTitle: Basic-fit spectrum allocation for Elastic Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Now-a-days huge growth in network applications in the field of mobile technology, cloud computing, data center network and social networks has led to requirements for high speed networks. To fulfill such wide range of requirements one of the promising solution is optical networks. WDM is one such technology whose bandwidth can be enhanced up to 100Gbps by effectively utilizing the fiber. However once the traffic demand varies WDM aren't effective, hence an effective solution is required for handling varying data traffic demands. Most appropriate solution for this case is utilization of elastic optical networks (EONs) which provide huge bandwidth by using spectrum as fine orthogonal subcarriers but extra constraints need to be considered while allotting subcarriers using Routing and Spectrum allocation (RSA) of EONs. The main objective of this work is to analyze basic-fit allocations such as first-fit, random-fit and exact-fit spectrum allocations and introduce fragment aware routing algorithm. The routing method is compared with shortest path spectrum reuse algorithm (SPSR) and balanced load spectrum allocation (BLSA) routing algorithm. The basic-fit spectrum allocations are implemented to these routing techniques.

articleTitle: A Novel 5Gbps PIN based Photo Receiver circuit employing External Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A novel high sensitive PIN based photo detector circuit has been designed and tested with external laser modulation configurations for data rate of 5Gbps with Clock and Data Recovery circuit achieving a sensitivity of -26dBm for a Bit Error Ratio (BER) > 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>. To the best of our knowledge this is best sensitivity achieved for the given data rate and BER. We have also explored the limitation imposed by switching speed on laser diode using direct modulation. A sensitivity of -29dBm was achieved up to 1.5Gbps.

articleTitle: Metal-Grating Assisted Surface Plasmon Resonance based Highly Sensitive Gas Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metal-grating assisted surface Plasmon resonance based highly sensitive refractive index sensor for the detection of gases in wavelength interrogation mode. The structural parameters are optimized to get high sensing performance. The sensitivity is observed to be 9000 nm/RIU (refractive index units) for the ambient refractive index in the range 1.00-1.01. The structural parameters have shown the tunability of the resonant wavelength, sensitivity and figure of merit of the sensor in a wide range.

articleTitle: Optimization of Tapered Fiber for the Compression of Femtosecond Pulses at Different Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We optimize tapering parameters of a large mode area W-fiber for the pulse compression of ultra-short high peak power pulses at three different wavelengths of 1550 nm, 1800 nm and 2000 nm. We study the dependence of tapering and fiber length on pulse compression with an input pulse of 100 kW and 250 fs. We achieve the maximum compression at 65% tapering and 35 cm fiber length for all the three wavelengths. This fiber can be an excellent choice for high power applications such as remote sensing, spectroscopy and medical treatments in a wide wavelength range.

articleTitle: Toroidal Resonances in Graphene Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Toroidal dipoles, unlike electric and magnetic dipoles, are formed due to currents flowing on the surface of a torus along it's meridians. Using numerical simulations, we investigate toroidal resonances in a graphene based 2D terahertz metamaterial structure. We further examine the effect of symmetric split gaps on the toroidal resonance response in the proposed metamerial structure. The excitation and control of toroidal resonance can be significant in the design of modulators, filters and sensors.

articleTitle: Implications of SBS Assisted Slow-Light in One-rod Core Chalcogenide MOF
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We elucidate attributes of the slow-light facilitated by stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in chalcogenide (As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) glass based one-rod core microstructured optical fiber (MOF). Our theoretical results comprise the assessment of Brillouin gain spectrum, Brillouin gain coefficient and Brillouin frequency shift by taking into account of acoustic mode. The time-delay up to 137.1ns can be accomplished from 1m length of fiber with pump power of 100mW. Our theoretical results nominate that slow-light can be adapted by tailoring the structural parameters of an MOF, and thereby tunable slow-light features can be acquired.

articleTitle: Optical Weight Measurement System Using FBG based Edge Filter Detection Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Fiber Bragg Gratings (FBGs) are known for their excellent strain and temperature sensing capability. In this manuscript, application of FBG in weight measurement system is explored and investigated. FBG based optical load cell is designed and tested for the load capacity of upto 5kg. The FBG sensing data is converted in optical power variation using edge filter detection based interrogation technique. Where, the transmission spectra of FBG is smartly used as edge filter and sensing element that makes this system a low cost solution. The system sensitivity is calculated to 99.6mV/kg which is almost twice that of calculated sensitivity of conventional electronic load cell. Hysteresis effect on FBG based optical load cell is also analyzed. Nominal changes in output voltages during loading and unloading process is observed. This suggests that this load cell has low hysteresis error with high repeatability. Thus, the realized optical load cell can be a good substitute for electronic sensor in this capacity range.

articleTitle: Degeneracy of Dark C points
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Polarization singularities are point singularities in vector fields where azimuth of polarization ellipse is not defined. C points and V points are generic polarization singularities. We report here the degeneracy present in dark C point polarization singularities. Dark C points of same index and polarization distribution can be generated using different combinations of orthogonally circularly polarized vortex beams and hence these are degenerate. We also discuss some of the possible methods for lifting the degeneracy of dark C points. Simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Picosecond Fundamental Soliton Pulse Compression in Self-similarly designed Chalcogenide Taper Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate a pulse compression scheme to compress picosecond fundamental soliton at 2500 nm using Self-similarly designed chalcogenide tapered photonic crystal fiber. Exponentially decreasing dispersion along the length of the fiber act as a tool for the compression process. Dynamics of propagating fundamental soliton has been studied by utilizing nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Quality analysis has also been investigated for different fiber length to achieve efficient compression condition to achieve high quality IR regime pulses.

articleTitle: Light Propagation Characteristics of a Tapered Double Clad LMA Fiber with Near Diffraction Limited Output
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A fiber taper based mode-field adaptor (MFA) and pump coupling component have been designed to transmit signal and cladding pump power in between single mode fiber and double clad large mode area fiber (DC-LMA) avoiding mode field mismatch and coupling loss. The signal and cladding power transmission has been characterized for a tapered DC-LMA for a set of taper lengths and angles. The designed MFA of taper length of 12 mm is having a near diffraction limited beam of M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ~ 1.023 along with efficient signal transmission.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Laser-patterned and Au-coated Iron Surfaces as SERS Platforms for Multiple Analytes Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report a single-step approach for fabricating nanogrooves and ripple-like surface structures on iron (Fe) substrate using femtosecond laser irradiation in acetone and different laser processing conditions. Subsequently, these laser-patterned Fe surfaces were used as SERS sensors post deposition of a thin gold (Au) film. The Au coated laser-patterned Fe surface structures exhibited superior detection limits for the dye methylene blue (5 nM) and a pesticide (thiram, 10 μM) with enhancement factor (EFs) of ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>.

articleTitle: Dual Ring Resonator for Gas sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Design of dual ring resonator structure has been proposed based on Silicon-on-insulator technology for gas sensing. When the structure is functionalized with polymer layers as a cladding layer then refractive index of the guided mode in the ring resonator is modified.

articleTitle: Mitigation of thermally induced non-linear effects in silicon ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a detailed experimental study of the mitigation of two-photon absorption (TPA) in a silicon micro ring modulator. TPA induced free-carrier absorption results in interesting optoelectronic process in silicon ring resonators. In this work, we study the effect of optical and RF power on the spectral characteristics of a ring modulator. In particular, we report the evolution of optical bistability in the transmission spectrum with free carriers and thermally induced refractive index change.

articleTitle: Modulating dual-band electromagnetically induced transparency effect via near field coupling in planar terahertz metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this article, we numerically and analytically investigate a metamaterial (MM) geometry comprising of a Cut-wire (CW) and a pair of asymmetric double C shaped resonators (DCRs) capable of exhibiting dual-band electromagnetically induced transparency effect. The dual-band EIT effect in the proposed MM results from the strong near field coupling between the bright mode resulting from the CW and pair of dark modes resulting from the two DCRs. The configuration allows us to modulate the transparency windows by displacing one DCR w.r.t the CW and keeping the other fixed. The study could be significant in the development of multi-band slow light devices, buffers and modulators.

articleTitle: Large and controllable light-induced shift of the longitudinal surface plasmon resonance of gold nanorods submerged in hydroquinone solution
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrates light-activated tuning of the longitudinal surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of gold nanorods submerged in hydroquinone solution. The LSPR exhibits a light-controlled red-shift of more than 100 nm, but only under continuous illumination. It is also possible to return to the starting LSPR value by washing the nanorods with cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide solution.

articleTitle: Qubit Network Barriers to Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The popularity of artificial neural networks (ANNs) of great depth and Quantum computing have led to many speculations as to their convergence. We enumerate barriers to utilizing qubit networks for deep learning architectures. We also describe the criteria for an effective usage of qubit networks and then assert that the bottleneck in their implementation is a lack of quantum algorithms for utilizing the topology of a deep neural network.

articleTitle: Power Analysis of Photonic Sensor for Detection of E-coli in Water
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The optical photonic crystal sensor design is proposed, which contains Silicon (Si) circular rods, made in a square lattice structure. The input point has a light source of wavelength 1.55um and has two output points to observe the output. The paper proposed different Photonic Crystal structure and power analysis for the same. The calculation for change in Refractive index value and power - wavelength shift for Water(1.33 RI) and E-coli (1.388 RI bacteria in water) analyte is analyzed and plotted. The procedure repeated for proposed different structures. Using a new design of 2D slab, we have observed the power output, amplitude and quality factor for different structure. The quality factor for proposed structure is observed and Cantilever structure is giving very high quality factor of 25954.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Microwave Photonic Filter for Digital Modulation Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Microwave photonic filters are extensively explored for their capability to filter high frequency microwave signals. In this paper, performance analysis of a coherent photonic filter for digital data communication is conducted. The performance analysis is done by using digital modulation and demodulation techniques to observe the effect of various optical components on signal recovery in electrical domain. It investigates digital modulation scheme i.e. 8-DPSK for 1.5 Gbps data rate. The performance analysis is based on constellation diagram, eye diagrams and received optical power. Minimum receiving power is calculated for optimal probability of error.

articleTitle: Effect of sensing layer thickness on the performance of a reduced Graphene oxide based Photon detector
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Reduced graphene oxide based Field Effect Transistors are fabricated and tested for photon detection in the wavelength range of 100-280 nm. The paper reports a study to analyze the effect of reduced graphene oxide layer thickness on the performance of the detector. Also, the detector showed deteriorated performance after one month of fabrication, a portion of which could be restored by low temperature vacuum annealing.

articleTitle: Optical Response of a Subwavelength Grating Waveguide Loaded With a Plasmonic Nanoantenna
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Single plasmonic-nanoparticle sensing holds a great promise in ultra-small analyte volume detection. Waveguide-loading is a simple way to achieve single nanoantenna interrogation in comparison to free-space configurations. Previously, we have reported the optical behaviour of dielectric waveguides loaded with simple and compound plasmonic-nanoantennae and the refractive index sensing performance of this setup[12]. Here, we extend this work by replacing dielectric waveguide with a SWG waveguide to improve the coupling efficiency. The numerical study shows that the coupling efficiency is doubled and sensitivity is improved considerably for refractive index sensing. This geometry promises on-chip applications like refractive index sensing and small footprint attenuators.

articleTitle: Exploring polarization independent plasmon induced transparency in a planar terahertz metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We numerically examine plasmon induced transparency (PIT) in planar terahertz metamaterials comprising of four U-shaped resonators and a cross-wire like structure. The plasmon induced transparency effect is studied for two orthogonal polarization of incident terahertz radiation. The proposed geometry is found to exhibit strong PIT effect for both the polarizations indicating a polarization independent response to the incident terahertz. It is further observed that the transparency window can be modulated based upon the positioning of U-shaped resonators from the cross-wire structure.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Enhanced Photoluminescence in p-doped GaAs using Fluorescence Lifetime Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The realization of low threshold, room temperature operation of semiconductor NIR nanolasers is still a challenge. Large surface-to-volume ratio of the nanostructures aggravates surface recombination leading to non-radiative decay of excited carriers. P-doping of active material is a viable solution to bring down the lasing threshold without surface passivation. Here, we report an improved quantum yield of p-doped GaAs over intrinsic, with the help of carrier lifetime measurement using FLIM system. We aim to study how the onset of the Auger process affects the PL and carrier lifetime at higher pump fluence.

articleTitle: Simulation of Terahertz Propagation by TE Mode in Metal Dielectric Metal Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We examine the propagation of terahertz multimode in a metal dielectric metal (MDM) waveguide. In this structure, terahertz radiation propagates through the vacuum region sandwiched by two thin metal plates. At terahertz frequencies metallic plates acts as a perfect electric conductor. Different modes like transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) and multiple modes propagate which depends upon the plate separation and polarisation of incident wave. The TE mode propagation is studied analytically and numerically. Another structure where metallic plates are replaced by semiconductor plates, Surface Plasmon Polariton (SPP) modes are observed propagating through the waveguide. The proposed study is important in developing terahertz devices, such as sensors and modulator.

articleTitle: Evaluation of cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin films grown at different annealing temperatures for efficient terahertz generation
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The paper reports the terahertz generation from polycrystalline CdTe thin films using 800 nm wavelength of 35 fs pulse duration at 1 kHz repetition rate obtained from Ti: sapphire laser amplifier. These films were deposited by thermal evaporation on a glass substrate and annealed at 200 and 300°C. The structural was investigated by XRD technique. Absorbance and transmittance were recorded in the wavelength (300- 800 nm). Optical studies showed that the optical energy gap decreases with increasing annealing temperatures. The results show that the film annealed at 200°C shows the highest generation of the order of 88 nW.

articleTitle: Low temperature PECVD deposited Silicon Nitride grating couplers with high efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report and demonstrate high efficiency grating couplers on PECVD deposited Silicon Nitride films. The couplers were fabricated on a 400 nm thick film that was embedded in a SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> cladding. The experimentally measured coupling efficiency was -5.6 dB per coupler for gratings on a Silicon substrate and -2.58 dB per coupler for gratings with a bottom Bragg reflector. The reported efficiencies are comparable to similarly deposited stacks using LPCVD based processes.

articleTitle: Amorphous Germanium for Mid Infrared Photonics
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a low-temperature plasma-enhanced-chemical-vapor-deposition of amorphous germanium films for Mid-infrared photonics. A film transparency of 3.2 to 8 μm with a minimum average roughness of 0.26 nm is achieved by tuning the deposition parameters.

articleTitle: Self-Focusing of Quadruple Gaussian Laser Beam in Relativistic Plasma using Moment Theory Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present paper, propagation characteristics of quadruple Gaussian laser beam in a relativistic plasma has been investigated using moment theory approach. Second order non-linear differential equation has been formulated analytically in the presence of relativistic non-linearity. The propagation of beam width parameter for a particular set of parameters has been studied with the distance of propagation. Effect of plasma density, laser beam intensity and lateral beam separation is discussed graphically. We have found that the incremental of normalized plasma density and lateral beam separation enhance the focusing effect. The conclusions obtained are applicable in high harmonic generation, X-ray generation and inertial confinement fusion (ICF).

articleTitle: 500 W Ytterbium Doped Monolithic Fiber Laser at 1 µm using Non-Wavelength Stabilized Laser Diodes
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper we report a Ytterbium doped fiber laser delivering a power of 486 W at 1074 nm with a SNR of 45 dB by using non-wavelength stabilized (NWS) laser diodes. The difficulties of using such NWS laser diodes are briefly stated and consequences of using such laser diodes in high power cavity are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Guiding Attributes of Square Lattice Microstructured Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We elucidate guiding characteristics of modified hexagonal lattice microstructured optical fibres (MOFs) which are popularly, known as the MOFs with square lattice of air-holes (SL-MOFs) in the cladding. An alternative analytical field model is utilized to explore the radical propagation attributes of SL-MOFs. For comparison numerical results based on the finite element method are also generated for the same model. Coherent agreement between the results is achieved, which justifies the strength of our approximate method; moreover, it furnishes a swift approach for exploring the fundamental modal properties of such optical waveguides.

articleTitle: Study of Gap Plasmons in 2D Finite Metal-Insulator-Metal Tunnel Junctions
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The electrical excitation of surface plasmons/photons from MIM tunnel junctions has attracted significant research attention in recent times [1]-[3]. These devices, though are promising for future on-chip plasmonic applications, are plagued with low quantum efficiencies. In an effort towards increasing the effectiveness of such devices, we study the behaviour of gap plasmons in Ag-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-Ag and Al-Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Au structures, with a 3 nm oxide and confined in two dimensions. We find that the out-coupling of leaky modes due to the Fabry-Pérot resonances in the oxide region contributes to the lower efficiencies of MIM tunnel junctions.

articleTitle: Quantitative phase imaging of MG63 cancer cells for monitoring changes in morphology with time using spatially low and temporally high coherent light source
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In the present work, we have synthesized pseudo- thermal light source and developed the speckle-free quantitative phase interferometric microscope which can be utilized to determine various biological parameters such as morphology, phase, refractive index, cell density etc. We have obtained the phase images of the cultured MG63 cancer cells at different time points for the quantification of different cell stages after seeding. Small changes in the morphology cannot be distinguished using bright field and fluorescence microscopy. But the technique presented in this paper, can quantify morphology and shape of the cell easily.

articleTitle: Femtosecond transient grating studies in CS2
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We explore transient grating formation in CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with femtosecond pulses. The spatially periodic excitation changes the nonlinear refractive index of the medium periodically, resulting in diffraction of the probe beam. The pump power dependence of the self-diffraction efficiency shows a second order power-law indicating the process involving a third-order nonlinearity. Time-resolved diffraction of the probe beam measured with a photodiode gives the third-order autocorrelated signal. CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> having large third order nonlinearity in a broad range of wavelengths in the visible and near-infrared, is proposed to be a promising candidate for measuring the pulse-widths for pulses generated from optical parametric amplifiers (OPA) using this technique.

articleTitle: Compact Tapers for Wire-to-Slot Fundamental Mode Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a compact taper-based scheme for a wire-to-slot waveguide coupler in Silicon-on-Insulator platform. The phase matching between a wire and slot mode is achieved using a ~17.5 μm compact fabrication-tolerant multimode interference-based taper. We show a theoretical wire-to-slot coupling efficiency of 90 % and fabricate the devices to obtain a coupling of ~6.4 dB per coupler.

articleTitle: Spectrum Analysis of Ytterbium-Doped Hybrid Mode-Locked Fiber Laser
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We emphasis the impact of spectrum in the ytterbium-doped fiber lasers with the nonlinear polarization rotation (NPR) saturable absorber (SA), transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) SA and hybrid SA (combination of both NPE and TMD). The numerical modeling of the pulse propagation inside the fiber cavity is based on the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.

articleTitle: Study of Starch Using Bright Field and Polarized Light Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Starch is a polymer derived from plants that have various applications. There are various types of starch available like potato, maize, tapioca, and wheat, etc. We have studied and successfully differentiated tapioca and maize starch using polarized light microscopy and bright field techniques with the help of Iodine staining. Starch granules are suspended in aqueous or non-aqueous media for polarized light and bright field microscopy. The botanical source of the starch is identified according to the shape and size of granules, granule surface marking, the position of hilum, iodine staining, and the presence of maltase crosses under polarized light.

articleTitle: Diffractive Resonant Radiation in Chirped Waveguide Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We investigate the propagation of discrete spatial soliton in a chirped waveguide array with generation and evolution of diffractive radiation. We track the evolution of the soliton in the Fourier Domain and try to numerically predict the position of the generated radiation through the phase matching condition for which energy transfer takes place between the soliton and radiation.

articleTitle: Effect of Silver and Gold on SPR Based D-shaped Photonic Crystal Fiber Refractive Index Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a D-shaped photonic crystal fiber refractive-index sensor using SPR and investigate the effect of silver and gold as plasmonic materials. The sensing characteristics are analyzed using finite element method and maximum sensitivity of 10,000nm/RIU is obtained for gold.

articleTitle: Laser Induced Cavitation Bubble Dynamics from Twin Breakdown Sites
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Laser induced breakdown in liquid or solid-liquid interface leads plasma formation which in later stages is replaced by cavitation bubble. The laser induced breakdown also leads to formation of nanoparticles based on the selection of solid target and its affinity to surrounding liquid. We investigate here the possible role played by cavitation bubbles in altering the traits of nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of Silicon Photonic Waveguides at Mid-IR Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This paper presents the modal characteristics of silicon-on-sapphire (SOS) and silicon-on-nitride (SON) rib waveguides at mid-IR wavelengths (3-5 μm). The multimode to single mode transition for different waveguide widths has been determined numerically at different wavelengths. The Payne-Lacey (P-L) model has been used to calculate the scattering loss. It has been observed that lower scattering loss is obtained for larger rib widths at lower wavelengths and smaller rib width at larger wavelengths. SOS waveguides have better mode confinement and lower scattering loss than SON waveguides.

articleTitle: Dynamic deformation analysis using diffraction phase microscopy and space-frequency analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, graphics processing unit (GPU) assisted windowed Fourier transform algorithm is used to process interferograms obtained in diffraction phase microscopy for noninvasive measurement of dynamic deformation undergone by a test specimen under variable load. The practical viability of our approach is shown by measuring the dynamic out of plane displacement of a glass slide sample coated with Aluminum thin film.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an Optical 1:2 Demultiplexer Using Micro Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Recently Micro Ring Resonator (MRR) have found its application in designing optical logic gates. This paper describes the working of a demultiplexer using MRRs. MRR behaves as a powerful optical switching device. Due to this, realization of AND gate and NOT gate has been proposed by appropriate arrangements of the MRRs. The combination of optical AND and optical NOT gates helps in the realization of 1:2 optical demultiplexer. The area of the simulated 1:2 Optical Demultiplexer design is approximately 16000 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The design has been carried out according to the existing semiconductor foundries capability.

articleTitle: Numerical studies on a single quantum well with and without electric field
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The electron and hole energy levels in a Al-GaAs/GaAs quantum-well structure is numerically studied. The quantum well without applied electric field is analyzed using matrix approach in which the well and barrier layers are modelled as stacks of thin layers as described by [1]. The quantum well is then subjected to an applied electric field, and the particle energies are calculated by using exact solution of Schrodinger equation [2] which involves Airy functions, and the obtained values are compared to that obtained using [1]. The results show that the difference in the energy values calculated using the two techniques matches very well only at higher electric fields.

articleTitle: Random lasing from amplifying electrostatic spray of charged microjets
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate random lasing in an amplifying electrostatic spray of charged microjets. Upon optical excitation with picosecond laser pulses, the chaotic liquid jets support random lasing modes at arbitrary wavelengths. These amplifying charged microjets can be applicable for white light random lasers.

articleTitle: Complementary Metamaterials Based Broadband Bandpass Terahertz Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We examine theoretically the broadband effects for terahertz frequency domain using complimentary resonators based metamaterials. The simulated outcomes clearly show broadband transparency window when operated in transmission mode.

articleTitle: Refractive Index sensing using plasmonic mode in a periodically corrugated waveguide at terahertz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the capability of a planar plasmonic waveguide to sense the refractive index. The waveguide is made up of one dimensional array of long grooved structures which exhibit resonant modes at terahertz frequency. To examine the various sensing parameters such as dispersion properties of the fundamental mode and frequency shift in modes, we varied the refractive index of analyte in long grooved structure. We confirm numerical findings with the theoretical model comprising of long grooves filled with analyte. The present study of plasmonic waveguide sensor could be significant in developing ultrasensitive terahertz thin film sensors.

articleTitle: SPR Sensor Based on Ag-metallized Nanolayer in One-rod Core Hexagonal Microstructured Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A surface plasmon resonance sensor (SPR) based on Ag-metallized nanolayer in the one-rod core microstructured optical fiber (MOF) is theoretically investigated with sensitivity of 1706nm/RIU. In contrast to traditional SPR sensors the performance of our proposed device is manifestly better.

articleTitle: Effect of M2 parameter of the fiber and the laser on the efficiency of coupling between them
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a study on the dependence of coupling efficiency between an optical fiber and a laser on their M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> factors viz. M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. It is observed that the coupling efficiency is maximum for M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/ M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><; 1. This gives a fair idea for selection of optical fibers in coupling laser beams to optical fibers.

articleTitle: Investigation of Light Absorption in Gold Nanoparticles Embedded Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskite Film
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We investigate the inclusion of gold-nanoparticles of different sizes, and concentrations as light absorption enhancers in methyl-ammonium lead iodide (MAPbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>) perovskite films, with the aim of establishing some guidelines for the future development of plasmonic resonance-based perovskite solar cells. We observe that the composite perovskite present the high light absorption coefficient for low concentration of gold-nanoparticles with small particles size. This study is important for the selection of matched concentration and size of gold or other metallic nanoparticles to design the efficient plasmon-enhanced organic-inorganic halide perovskite based solar cells and other optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Optical phase-locked loop based carrier phase recovery and compensation for 8-PSK coherent optical links
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Coherent optical links with analog and optical signal processing are expected to replace existing intensity modulation and direct detection based techniques in the near future for achieving energy efficiency in inter and intra data center interconnects. Carrier synchronization is one of the key challenges in these optical links. We propose an optical phase-locked loop based carrier offset compensation architecture for achieving synchronization in 8-PSK coherent optical links. The optical phase-locked loop uses a cross-correlator based phase detector with four-level quantizer and phase modulator for phase variations compensation. The system-level behavioral simulations show promising results for the 8-PSK links.

articleTitle: Group velocity dispersion in terahertz hollow-core hexagonal photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Hollow-core hexagonal photonic crystal (PhC) fiber for terahertz (THz) frequencies is realized. THz pulse propagation and transmission characteristics of the proposed PhC fiber are studied through full-wave electromagnetic computations. Including the out of plane-radiation losses, the proposed fiber exhibits transmission of more than 97.7% for transverse electric (TE) polarization at 0.210 THz for hexapole-like mode. The pulse propagation suggests the group velocity dispersion in the PhC fiber. The present work finds applications in the development of THz communication systems.

articleTitle: Development of micro dye laser based on micro wire molding technique
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Three dimensional microfluidic dye laser inside PDMS has been fabricated by microwire molding technique. Visible laser emission from micro-laser was achieved in a micro-laser of 1mM R6G dye dissolved in a mixture of ethanol and benzyl alcohol as the active medium. The laser output intensity profile and variation of the output with the pump power was studied and a threshold of 4.5 mW pump power was observed.

articleTitle: All-Dielectric Metasurfaces for Reflection and Transmission-Mode Color Filter Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report all-dielectric metasurface color filters working in reflection and transmission mode. The reflection mode filters are made by a-Si cylindrical nanopillars on top of a silica substrate, whereas the transmission mode filter structures are complementary in nature, i.e. holes on the poly-Si layer. The experimental results show that in reflection mode, it is possible to design pixels of 0.5μm profile. Also the numerical study shows that going beyond conventional uniform shapes, it is possible to enhance the performance parameters of the spectral filters.

articleTitle: Microwave Photonic System For Ultrawideband Waveform Generation Based on Photonic Microring Resonator and Electrical Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A microwave photonic system based on microring resonator and electrical filter for generating ultrawideband waveforms is proposed and analyzed in a simulation environment. These waveforms are obtained by varying the bandwidth, order of filter and timestep, number of samples of electrical signal resampler. UWB waveforms covering the 3.1 - 4.8 GHz band of the UWB spectrum are obtained for a sixth order bandpass filter of bandwidth 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Intensity modulator based on femtosecond laser assisted waveguide fabrication inside X-cut LiNbO3 crystal
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This work represents the development of waveguide based linear intensity modulator in X-cut LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> wafer. We report on fabrication of optical waveguide structures in X-cut lithium niobate crystal with femtosecond laser direct writing method. Change in refractive index profile is measured using near field intensity profile measurement method for the optimized writing condition. It has been observed that change refractive index (Δn) is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> and the corresponding electro-optic effect at 632.8 nm and 1550 nm is also measured by patterning electrode structure on the substrate. Experimental results indicate that this scheme can be further improved for achieving optical waveguide- based high-speed modulators, optical sensors on X-cut LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> crystal.

articleTitle: Study of temperature and hydrostatic pressure effect on SHG associated with the excitonic system in an InN Quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Here, the study of SHG for the correlation of electron- hole in an InN in a semi-parabolic quantum dot with external parameters temperature and hydrostatic pressure has been carried out using effective mass approximation. The density matrix formulations have been used to calculate the eigenvalues and Eigen energies. The dependence of Optical Rectification Coefficient (ORC) on the temperature and hydrostatic pressure in the strong confinement regime for both excitonic as well as without excitonic effects has been investigated. It was found that the ORC is strongly influenced by electron-hole pair localization, temperature change, and alteration in radius and variation in hydrostatic pressure.

articleTitle: A simple tri-layer metamaterial absorber for large area fabrication
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a simple metamaterial absorber suitable for large areas fabrication based on the cavity and guided-mode resonance. The absorber consists of tri-layer of gold, ZnS and gold on the photoresist micro-structures. The micro-structures were fabricated using laser interference lithography and followed by the sequential deposition of the tri-layer using physical vapour deposition technique. Due to the tri-layer on the structured photoresist, there is a formation of cavity and waveguide which enable absorption of the electromagnetic radiation at some specific frequencies. Our proposed design provides polarization and wide-angle insensitive electromagnetic response. The metamaterial absorbers were also characterized for their emissivity.

articleTitle: Lasing based on periodically patterned anisotropic thin film metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We study random lasing from Rhodamine 6G dye infiltrated into a periodically patterned, anisotropic thin film metamaterial. The periodic anisotropy is created by depositing silver nanocolumnar structures on a diffraction grating. The nanocolumnar structures provide the required optical feedback for the lasing.

articleTitle: Power Requirement Estimation of Directed Energy System for Static and Dynamic Target
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Directed Energy System (DES) is highly efficient to damage both static and dynamic targets. Each target demands a minimum lethal fluence to make engagement successful, depending on the material, thickness, coating and structural properties. DES provides the required lethal fluence on the target to reach the melting or burning temperature. The static target consumes approximately constant fluence, but for the dynamic target, the flux density requirement estimation varies within the dwell time, which is proportional to the distance between the DES and the target. In this paper, the initial power requirement of DES has been estimated based on target specification.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of conflict of different homing heads of target locator with mid infrared source
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The two major homing head guidance system used in the history are spin-scan and con-scan reticle based modulators. The working principles for both scanning techniques are different. In this paper the simulation of the target on the Target Locator (TL) reticle has been done with the help of MATLAB. Here target locator is a projectile moving towards target to neutralize it. The sampling rate has been taken as base reference to draw and analyse the variation in the movement of the nutating and rotating circle. The period of nutation and rotation is expressed as number of cycle.

articleTitle: Micro-channeled Single Mode Fiber Plasmonic Sensor with ITO-TiO2 Bilayer
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A microchannel incorporated single mode fiber plasmonic sensor coated with ITO-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> bilayer is proposed in this paper. The sensor responds over a wide refractive index range from 1.33 to 1.41 and sensitivity of 10500nm/RIU is obtained for refractive index 1.41.

articleTitle: Hybrid Waveguide Platform for Integrated Photonics Application
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a versatile waveguide configuration that offers a widely tunable waveguide dispersion. The waveguide is formed by sandwiching high-index silicon between medium-index silicon nitride. We demonstrate grating couplers for both TE and TM mode with efficiency of -3.27 and -8 dB per coupler respectively and also demonstrate a ring resonator with a Q-factor of 3400 and a maximum extinction of 30 dB.

articleTitle: Selective Absorption of Visible Light by Blood for Vein Visualizing Aid
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Venepunctures in neonates and senior citizens is challenging for phlebotomists. Large range of expensive infrared light based products are available which involve complex algorithms to project the vein pattern on the skin but do not provide depth information. Other vein devices use red light for such vein visual enhancement where eye sensitivity is low. We optimized the visual response as well as both oxy-, deoxy- haemoglobin absorption to achieve better performance. The designed prototype for vein vizualisation uses light emitting diodes that provide visual contrast through diffuse light for the vein against the background tissue by relying on selective absorption.

articleTitle: Broadband Source for Optical Coherence Tomography at 1064 nm Using Silica-based Microstructured Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Supercontinuum spectra are generated using microstructured optical fibers (MOFs) fabricated indigenously for utilization as broadband source in ultrahigh-resolution optical coherence tomography. The MOFs have different structural, dispersive and nonlinear properties, thus generating SC spectra with different bandwidths when pumped anomalously at 1064 nm. For all the MOFs, theoretically determined axial resolution shows improvement than existing sources. Theoretical axial resolution of 0.678 µm was achieved from one of the MOFs which is one of the lowest values till now. Hence our MOFs can be used as efficient broadband source in OCT to obtain ultrahigh axial resolution in the sub-micron level.

articleTitle: Refractive Index Sensitivity Enchantment of a Fiber Filter by MZI Cascaded Sagnac Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A novel technique to enhance the sensitivity of single-fiber (SF) MZI based refractive index sensor is presented. An indigenously fabricated SF-MZI has been placed in MZI cascaded Sagnac interferometer fiber loop and its sensitivity is enhanced from 20.24 nm per RIU to 40.92 nm per RIU over a relatively large range from 1.3344 RIU to 1.4532 RIU.

articleTitle: Quantum cascade laser-based in situ measurement of atmospheric CO and CO2 in Gandhinagar using 1f and 2f wavelength modulation spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
