abstract: We report the design, development and field deployment of a quantum cascade laser-based tunable diode laser spectroscopy (TDLS) system for high-sensitivity measurement of atmospheric CO and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Two distributed-feedback quantum cascade lasers are used to interrogate the rotational-vibrational transitions of CO at 4594.99 nm and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at 4319.30 nm. The mean mole fraction values for CO and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> for the measurements made at Gandhinagar from 19-25 July 2019 are 477 ppb and 486 ppm respectively. The detection limit of the system is 3 ppb CO and 45 ppb CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> for integration time of 17 s and 69 s respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband and flat THz dispersion in biatomic photonic band gap fibers
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Teflon based biatomic photonic band gap fiber was studied and its bandwidth was calculated using full vector plane wave expansion method. Optimizations were carried out by changing the ratio between two adjacent air holes in the cladding triangular lattice. The modal fields for guided spectrum were calculated using finite element method. The transmission spectrum and zero dispersion wavelengths, both are found to be sensitively dependent on the holes diameter ratio. The dispersion curves are almost flat covering from normal to anomalous dispersion region. Such dispersion characteristics can be used for generation of THz supercontinuum generation by filling hollow core of the fiber with a suitable nonlinear medium.

articleTitle: Improved Polarisation Filter Design Using Modified Photonic Crystal Fiber Based on Surface Plasmon
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a simple design for realizing a polarization filter using photonic crystal fiber. This design consists of four small low-index air-holes close to the fiber core and single gold ring around its center hole. The bandwidth performance of filter is numerically analyzed by varying the diameters of small air-holes. Surface plasmon resonance occurs at 1.55 μm resonance wavelength where coupling arises due to the phase matching between the silica core mode and surface plasmon mode. The proposed design offers high bandwidth of ~520 nm and resonance strength of 562 dB/cm which is suitable for a miniature polarization device.

articleTitle: Commercial DVDs loaded with Femtosecond Laser Prepared Gold Nanoparticles as SERS Substrates
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A simple, readily available SERS substrate was investigated by utilizing the metallic layer of commercially available DVDs. The channel-like regions could trap metal NPs creating ‘hotspots". Au nanoparticles fabricated using fs laser ablation technique were used.

articleTitle: Thermal Inflection Study of Methanol-Hexane Mixtures using Time-Resolved Thermal Lens Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Time-resolved thermal lens (TL) technique is used to measure the heat transfer in pure methanol and its binary mixtures with hexane. We used dual-beam mode mismatched pump-probe scheme where a femtosecond laser beam of 1560 nm was used as a pump beam, and its frequency-doubled 780 nm beam was used as probe beam. TL Signal decreases with increasing concentration of hexane in the binary mixture. On higher concentration of Hexane in binary mixture then we have found convective heat transfer mode was absent. At 40%-60% methanol hexane mixture, we observed a sudden curious jump in TL signal.

articleTitle: Determining orbital angular momentum of light by analyzing interferogram with conjoined fork-like structures
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Light beam with helical wavefront carries well-defined orbital angular momentum (OAM) specified by its topological charge (TC). The off-axis self-interference of laterally displaced vortex beams results into interferogram consisting of pair of fork-like structures. In this study, it has been demonstrated that the interferogram consisting of conjoined fork-like structures allow simpler and unambiguous way of determining the sign and magnitude of TC carried by incoming vortex beam using interferogram analysis method. The method uses a Mach-Zehnder interferometer to introduce lateral displacement and tilt angles between the interfering beams.

articleTitle: Study of resonant modes for sensing in a multimode planar plasmonic terahertz waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We examine the refractive index sensing capability of the resonant modes in a planar plasmonic terahertz (THz) waveguide. The waveguide is comprised of one dimensional array of periodically arranged rectangular subwavelength grooves. The waveguide configuration supports resonant surface modes at certain frequencies depending on groove parameters and the refractive index of analyte filled in them. The change in refractive index leads to a linear shift in the fundamental as well as higher order modes for fixed parameters of the waveguide structures. Sensitivity and corresponding figure of merit (FoM) of terahertz modes are calculated to analyse the performance of the device.

articleTitle: Tuning of optical properties of Cu doped BTO thin films fabricated by PLD Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Pure BTO and Cu-BTO thin films are fabricated onto quartz substrate via PLD technique. Linear and nonlinear optical characterization of the thin films are carried out by using UV-Vis-NIR Spectrometer and modified Z-scan technique using cw Ar-Ion Laser at 488 nm wavelength, respectively. Effect of inclusion of Cu layer on BTO host matrix on absorbance and nonlinear optical properties have been studied.

articleTitle: Displacement sensing using terahertz metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel platform for displacement sensing at Terahertz (THz) frequency domain using symmetric metasurfaces. Our proposed device consists of periodic array of vertically stacked sub-wavelength dipole rods. Fano resonance possesses sharp asymmetric line shape, low radiation loss and large tuning capability. By exploiting above characteristics, our proposed device can be able to detect both lateral and rotational displacement of meta-resonators. Our concepts and results can be highly beneficial to realize active flexible meta-sensors with microelectromechanical tuning capability and in other commercial functional THz devices.
